items.note: Deliberation 2025-443 (PDF read) supports: régie with financial autonomy and legal personality, created by deliberation of 5 April 2004 as Parcub, now Metpark; runs 'une trentaine de parcs (de propriété métropolitaine et autres)'; statutes give it all Métropole public car parks except those under DSP. It does NOT give the 1 January 2020 renaming date (that date appears only in a different deliberation, 2025-319). Date 2020-01 is therefore not supported by this source.
items.corrected_text: METPARK is Bordeaux Métropole's own parking authority, a public body with its own legal personality and financial autonomy, set up in 2004 under the name Parcub. It runs about thirty car parks, and its statutes give it all of the Métropole's public car parks except those let out under public-service concessions.

items.note: Press kit p.21 ('Parkings, une tendance au repli', délibération 81): report of parking concession holders presented to councillors; 16,384 car spaces in 2023 (Métropole car parks or run by the régie, incl. 2 private ones); régie 29 sites / 11,849 spaces vs 5 concession sites / 3,693 spaces; hourly use 2023 -3.62% vs 2022; total revenue over EUR 36 million. Title and date correct.

Deliberation 2025-319 confirms closure since 28 Nov 2023 under an emergency safety order (shoring needed over loss of load-bearing capacity from visible beam corrosion), and the 15 M EUR TTC envelope over 4-5 years excluding car-park rehabilitation. But the council did not approve a plan to 'take over and repair' the deck: it authorised pursuing a symbolic-value acquisition of the deck (subject to agreement of all co-owners) and carrying out studies to define the works; the 15 M EUR is a provisional estimate 'susceptible de fortes variations', with programme and budget to come back to council in a later deliberation.
items.corrected_text: The METPARK car park at Front du Médoc has been closed since 28 November 2023, when an emergency safety order required shoring of corroded beams. In July 2025 the Métropole council authorised pursuing acquisition of the pedestrian deck above it, subject to the co-owners' agreement, and studies of repair works; the provisional budget, excluding repairs to the car park itself, is estimated at EUR 15 million over 4-5 years and may change considerably.

items.note: Baromètre 2024 p.6: 'le parking Gambetta a réouvert le 28 novembre 2024 après 10 mois de fermeture'; same page says Front du Médoc and Gambetta were closed for works.

Le Bonbon EN page (published 9 Dec 2024): EUR 7.8 million, 438 car spaces incl. 102 with charging (plus 28 motorcycle), ticketless entry/exit by licence-plate reading, intelligent guidance with dynamic panels showing available spaces in real time, reopened 28 November. Title matches. (This page says 'after a year of work', unlike the barometer's 10 months, but the item does not state a duration.)

Deliberation 2025-443: 1989 concession to Central Parc (Indigo) expires 1 Sept 2026; 336 spaces; ~109,400 hourly exits and 1.072 M EUR excl. tax revenue in 2024 - all supported. The council 'DECIDE d'adopter le principe' of returning it to METPARK management from 2 Sept 2026, with transfer terms left to a later deliberation, so 'decided that METPARK will run it' slightly overstates.
items.corrected_text: The 1989 concession under which Central Parc (Indigo group) runs the 336-space Camille Jullian underground car park ends on 1 September 2026, and the Métropole council approved in principle that METPARK take it over from 2 September 2026, with transfer terms to be set in a later decision. In 2024 it recorded about 109,400 hourly exits and revenue of EUR 1.07 million excluding tax.

items.note: The URL now 301-redirects to totalenergies.co.uk/news (no such release there). A WebSearch for the exact title returned the same page (evcharge.totalenergies.com/en/node/726) with its indexed text: 15-year contract, 1,500 charge points in 26 car parks, 1,420 + 40 at 7 kVA, 22 at 50 kW, 18 at 200 kW, parking waived for fast/high-power sessions under 30 minutes; a related index entry is dated 19/04/2024. Indexed text says the first charge points will begin supplying electricity from summer 2024, not that installation starts then.
items.corrected_text: METPARK awarded TotalEnergies a 15-year concession to install and run 1,500 charge points in 26 METPARK car parks, with the first points to supply power from summer 2024. Most are 7 kVA points, with 22 fast (50 kW) and 18 high-power (200 kW) chargers, and parking is to be free for fast-charging sessions under 30 minutes.

items.note: Baromètre 2025 p.7: 2,877 publicly accessible charge points, of which 958 in car parks (public and other). The 592 comparison figure is not in this report (it is in the 2024 barometer), and the report does not say 'end of 2025'.
items.corrected_text: Bordeaux Métropole's 2025 mobility report counted 958 publicly accessible charge points in car parks (public and other), out of 2,877 publicly accessible charge points in the area.

items.note: Press kit dated 6 Dec 2024 pp.5-6: ZFE 'entrera en vigueur' on 1 Jan 2025 intra-rocade (ring road excluded); bans non-classified vehicles; 2.1% of the fleet, ~11,000 vehicles; eleven P+R sites stay accessible; 24h ZFE pass, max 24 per year. All supported, but the source is a pre-announcement: it says the ZFE will come into force, not that it did.
items.corrected_text: Bordeaux Métropole's low-emission zone (ZFE) was due to come into force on 1 January 2025 inside the ring road, banning only vehicles with no Crit'Air rating, about 2.1% of the local fleet (around 11,000 vehicles). Eleven park-and-ride sites were to stay reachable for these vehicles, and a 24-hour ZFE pass can be used up to 24 times a year.

items.note: Athlon article (published 2 June 2026): Constitutional Council decision of 21 May 2026 struck the ZFE-abolition provision from the 'loi de simplification de la vie économique' as a cavalier législatif (insufficient link to the bill's purpose - procedural); 'Les ZFE restent donc juridiquement en vigueur'. Bordeaux not mentioned; item is worded as national and says so.

Banque des Territoires (20 Jan 2025): city hall announced on 17 Jan a 30% higher rate from 2 May for non-professional thermal cars >1,600 kg and hybrid/electric >1,900 kg, covering subscriptions and hourly rates, professional subscriptions exempt. Only 2 May appears (no 13 May), so 'May 2025' is supported. The last sentence (visitor page, EUR 51 vs EUR 39 FPS) is not on this page; those figures are on bordeaux.fr pages.
items.corrected_text: In January 2025 Bordeaux announced a 30% higher on-street parking rate from 2 May for petrol and diesel cars over 1,600 kg and hybrid or electric cars over 1,900 kg. It applies to hourly rates and subscriptions, but professionals' subscriptions are exempt.

items.note: bordeaux.fr article (updated 3 Aug 2026): changes 'ce début août 2026'; red and green zones replaced by a single zone; half-hour billing (previously quarter-hour); 30 free minutes once per day per vehicle; standard rates EUR 1.90 (45 min) to EUR 20.00 (4h); residents' system unchanged.

Same page: six Metpark car parks around the city centre free for 2 hours at weekends, 2,500 spaces combined. Names are not in the body text but are on the page's map image ('Carte des 6 parkings Metpark gratuits les week-ends'): Grand Parc, Beaujon, Porte de Bordeaux, Amédée Saint-Germain, Paludate, Amplitude. (Map notes Porte de Bordeaux closed for works until September 2026.)
FAQ page (updated 5 Oct 2026): paid 9h-19h except Sundays and public holidays; residents EUR 1/24h, 6/week, 10/fortnight, 15/month.

Le Bonbon (29 Sept 2026): Métropole 'prévoit' an average 3% rise in 2027 after 3.2% (2023), 3.6% (2024), 3% (2025); 'le parc-relais coûtera désormais 5€, contre 4,50€'. Framing as a press report / plan is appropriate (article mentions examination by metropolitan councillors but gives no vote). The page does not call it a 'day ticket'.
items.corrected_text: A press report says Bordeaux Métropole plans to raise TBM fares by an average of 3% in 2027, after average rises of 3.2% in 2023, 3.6% in 2024 and 3% in 2025. Under the plan, the park-and-ride fare goes from EUR 4.50 to EUR 5.

items.note: Baromètre 2024: hourly exits of 6 MetPark hypercentre car parks -2% vs 2023; subscribers also down (non-residents -6%, residents -2%); TBM validations +9%; road traffic -2% excluding ring road.

Baromètre 2025 p.6: hourly exits of 8 MetPark hypercentre car parks -3% vs 2024; 'depuis plusieurs années, la fréquentation horaire a diminué de 37%' - no start year given and the item does not imply one; non-resident subscribers -8%, residents -4%; TBM +3%.
bordeaux.fr 'Une attractivité confirmée' (18 Sept 2025): pedestrian sector enlarged from 172 to 259 ha in 5 years; footfall +15% in December 2024 vs December 2023 on city-centre shopping streets.

corrected_summary: METPARK, Bordeaux Métropole's own parking authority, runs about thirty car parks, and the Métropole council approved in principle that it take over the Camille Jullian car park when that concession ends in September 2026. Bordeaux Métropole's mobility reports show hourly use of METPARK hypercentre car parks down 2% in 2024 and 3% in 2025, while TBM transit validations rose. The ZFE low-emission zone was due to start on 1 January 2025, a 30% on-street surcharge for heavy cars was announced from May 2025, and from early August 2026 Bordeaux introduced a single paid zone, 30 free minutes a day and 2 free weekend hours in six METPARK car parks.
